newsitem.title: UK: British privatisations since 1980 -- at a glance.
newsitem.headline: British privatisations since 1980 -- at a glance.

text.p: Speculation is mounting about which British firms a possible Labour Government will target for a one-off "windfall" profits tax that according to media reports could raise up to 10 billion pounds ($16 billion).

Labour charges that a vast and controversial privatisation programme, spearheaded by Conservative former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher after winning office in 1979, short-changed consumers while leaving investors and executive "fat cats" of uncompetitive monopolies awash in cash.

Reuters has prepared a list of major privatisations since 1980 as rumours sweep the markets that Labour's tax net, if the party wins the election on May 1, will entangle more companies than those traditionally considered to be "privatised utilities".
The first part of the sale of British Telecommunications in 1984 eclipsed all other previous sell-offs.
Jaguar, British Leyland's luxury car unit 1984
National bus industry, separate regional sales 1986 to 1995
BP, UK sells last 31.7 pct stake * 1987
12 English and Welsh regional electricity companies 1990
3 ROSCO rail rolling stock leasing companies 1995

* NOTE - British Petroleum Co (BP) has been listed on the stock exchange since 1909. The government took a 66 percent stake in 1914 to secure oil supplies to the Navy during World War One. By October 1987, the state held just under 32 percent, most of which it then sold before disposing of its small remaining stake in 1996.

** NOTE - The National Grid was incorporated within the 12 regional electricity companies in 1990. It was demerged and separately floated on the stock exchange in December 1995. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
